privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what Codenames Online stores about you, why it is stored, and how long it is kept. Codenames Online is a student project built for the 42 curriculum, and it only collects what it needs to run accounts, matches and chat.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: Your account holds an email address, a username and a password. The password is never stored as plain text, only as a hash.

Your profile holds the avatar you pick from the preset set or upload. Playing matches adds your match history and the statistics derived from it, such as wins and losses. Using the social features adds your friend connections and the chat messages you send.

sections.title: Why we store it
paragraphs: Account data signs you in and identifies you to other players. Match results power your profile, your match history and your statistics. Friend connections and messages run the friends list and chat.
Your data is used only to run the game. Nothing is sold, rented or shared with advertisers.

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: Signing in sets two cookies: a short-lived session cookie and a refresh cookie that renews it. Both are HttpOnly, sent only to this site, and used for authentication alone.
Your language choice is saved in your browser's local storage, so the game opens in the same language next time. There are no advertising or analytics cookies.

sections.title: Live game data
paragraphs: Rooms, teams, roles, the board and the score live in temporary storage while a room is open, and are removed when the room closes.
If your connection drops, your seat is held for a short grace period so you can rejoin the same match. When a match ends, its result is added to the match history of every player in it.

sections.title: Chat messages
paragraphs: Room chat and direct messages between friends are kept for a limited period set by the server. Each message is deleted when that period ends.
Room messages are visible only to the players in that room, and direct messages only to the two friends in the conversation.

sections.title: What other players see
paragraphs: Signed-in players can see your username, your avatar, your online status and your public profile with its statistics. Players in the same room see your team, your role and your moves during a match.
The project does not share your data with third parties for advertising, marketing or any commercial purpose.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Account, profile, friend and match data stay while your account exists and the project's server is running. Chat messages are deleted when their retention period ends, and live room data is deleted when the room closes.

sections.title: Your choices
paragraphs: You can change your username and your avatar at any time, add or remove friends, and switch the interface language.
Changing your email address or password and deleting your account are not available inside the game. To have your account and its data removed, contact the project team.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Passwords are stored only as hashes, session cookies cannot be read by page scripts, and the deployed game is served over HTTPS. No system is perfectly secure, so avoid sharing sensitive personal information in your username, your avatar or your messages.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: This policy is updated when the game changes how it handles data. The date at the top of this page shows the current version.

sections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Questions and requests about your data go to the project team through the project repository.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms cover the use of Codenames Online. Creating an account means you accept them. The game is a student project built for the 42 curriculum and is offered for friendly play.

sections.title: About the game
paragraphs: Codenames Online is a real-time multiplayer word game. It offers accounts, profiles, game rooms, friends, chat, match history and statistics.
It is an independent educational project inspired by the Codenames board game. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Czech Games Edition or the Codenames brand.

sections.title: Your account
paragraphs: You need an account to play. Use an email address you control, pick a username that is not offensive or misleading, and keep your password to yourself. You are responsible for what happens under your account.

sections.title: Fair play
paragraphs: Play the game as designed. Do not pass hidden board information to Operatives outside the game, do not automate play, and do not manipulate results or statistics.
Do not try to access other accounts, disrupt rooms or the service, or exploit faults. If you find a fault, report it to the project team instead.

sections.title: Chat and conduct
paragraphs: Chat is for players in your room and for friends. Respect other players: harassment, hate speech, threats and spam are not allowed. You are responsible for the messages you send.
Do not leave or stall matches on purpose to spoil them for others. A room host can remove players from the room outside a running match.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: The game is a student project and is provided as it is. Connections can drop, matches can be interrupted, and the service can be unavailable during maintenance or once the project ends. There is no guaranteed uptime.
A dropped connection holds your seat for a short grace period. If you do not return in time, you leave the room.

sections.title: Your content
paragraphs: Your username, your avatar and your messages stay yours. The game stores only what it needs to run a match, show a profile and deliver chat, as described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: Intellectual property
paragraphs: The project's own code, interface design and artwork belong to the project team. Third-party libraries and fonts keep their own licenses. The Codenames name and the original game belong to their respective owners.

sections.title: Changes and ending use
paragraphs: These terms can change as the game develops, and the date at the top of this page shows the current version. You can stop using the game at any time. To have your account removed, contact the project team.

sections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Questions about these terms go to the project team through the project repository.
